title: Coastal Processes and Sediment Cells
welcome_lead: Stand on the shore and watch waves shape rock and sand into iconic coastal landforms.
meta_desc: IBDP Geography Adventure: coastal processes, longshore drift and sediment cells.
final_note: You have followed a grain of sand from cliff to spit. Coastal management must respect sediment systems.

concepts.def: Low, long waves with stronger swash than backwash, building beaches.
High, short waves with stronger backwash than swash, eroding beaches.
Movement of sediment along a coast in a zig-zag pattern under oblique waves.
Coastal compartment in which inputs, transfers and outputs of sediment can be considered as a closed system.
Depositional landform extending out from the coast where it changes direction.
Bar of sand or shingle connecting an island to the mainland.

walkthroughs.body_html: Wave energy depends on wind speed, duration and fetch. Constructive waves dominate in shelter and build beaches; destructive waves dominate in storms and erode them. Tides and currents modify wave action and influence depositional patterns.

Where waves approach the shore obliquely, swash carries sediment up the beach at an angle while backwash returns it directly down-slope, producing net movement along the coast (longshore drift). Groynes interrupt this movement to retain beach material.

England and Wales are divided into 11 major sediment cells, each comprising sources (cliffs, rivers), stores (beaches, dunes) and sinks (offshore deposits). Sustainable coastal management — shoreline management plans — must work at the cell scale rather than just plot by plot.
